methodology: Same-position Madden calibration with career/portrayal-specific play-style deltas. Busts model their college/draft prospect identity; fictional and crossover players use documented athletic traits. No random attribute adjustments are used.

players.name: Dee Milliner
players.build_note: Injuries limited the hoped-for Darrelle Revis successor to 21 games.

players.name: Justin Gilbert
players.build_note: Elite testing and ball skills did not survive effort, discipline, and consistency problems.

players.name: Steve Emtman
players.build_note: Considered a generational prospect at Washington; knee injuries wrecked him early.

players.name: Blair Thomas
players.build_note: Penn State runner selected ahead of multiple stars but never topped 728 rushing yards in a season.

ratings_basis.signature: Penn State home-run burst that never translated

players.name: Curtis Enis
players.build_note: Contract holdout drama followed by an unproductive, injury-shortened career.

ratings_basis.signature: Penn State power back, limited homerun speed

players.name: Ki-Jana Carter
players.build_note: Blew out his knee in the preseason and never recovered his college form.

players.name: Lawrence Phillips
players.build_note: Immense college talent at Nebraska, career derailed by off-field trouble.

players.name: Rashaan Salaam
players.archetype: HB / decorated college star + production profile
players.build_note: Heisman winner and 2,000-yard college rusher whose early promise faded quickly.

players.name: Ron Dayne
players.build_note: College football's career rushing king never became the franchise runner his draft slot suggested.

players.name: Trent Richardson
players.build_note: Alabama national champion who lost effectiveness almost immediately in the NFL.

players.name: Roberto Aguayo
players.build_note: Tampa Bay traded up for the famously accurate kicker, who lasted one season after making 71 percent of his field goals.

players.name: Dion Jordan
players.build_note: Length and movement skills never became pass-rush production, compounded by suspensions.

players.name: Aundray Bruce
players.build_note: The first linebacker ever selected first overall never approached franchise-player impact.

players.name: Greg Robinson
players.build_note: Exceptional power and athleticism never overcame technique and penalty issues.

players.name: Jason Smith
players.build_note: Concussions and inconsistency ended a once-promising tackle prospect's career early.

players.name: Luke Joeckel
players.build_note: Technically polished prospect who never became even an average long-term starter.

players.name: Robert Gallery
players.build_note: Elite tackle prospect who had to move inside after failing on the edge.

ratings_basis.signature: Iowa mauler who stalled in pass protection

players.name: Tony Mandarich
players.build_note: Infamous Sports Illustrated "The Incredible Bulk" cover; steroid-fueled hype collapsed in the NFL.

players.name: Akili Smith
players.build_note: Huge college hype at Oregon, never grasped an NFL playbook.

ratings_basis.signature: raw Oregon dual-threat traits, unfinished pocket game

players.name: Andre Ware
players.archetype: QB / spread distributor + decorated college star + production profile
players.build_note: Heisman-winning run-and-shoot star whose prolific college production never translated to an NFL starting career.

ratings_basis.signature: Heisman run-and-shoot distributor with real mobility

players.name: Brady Quinn
players.build_note: Notre Dame star and expected franchise passer who never became a stable NFL starter.

players.name: Dan McGwire
players.build_note: Mark McGwire's brother; a well-known name-recognition bust.

players.name: David Klingler
players.build_note: Prolific run-and-shoot college numbers didn't translate at all.

players.name: Heath Shuler
players.build_note: Highly touted Tennessee QB, out of the league within a few years.

players.name: JaMarcus Russell
players.build_note: The textbook modern draft bust — arm talent, work ethic and conditioning collapse.

ratings_basis.signature: historic arm talent, accuracy and conditioning drop-off

players.name: Johnny Manziel
players.archetype: QB / mobile quarterback + decorated college star + consistency concern
players.build_note: "Johnny Football" Heisman phenom; off-field issues turned a first-round pick into a two-year NFL cameo.

players.name: Josh Rosen
players.build_note: Polished UCLA prospect traded after one season and never recovered a starting opportunity.

ratings_basis.signature: polished UCLA timing passer, limited athlete

players.name: Matt Leinart
players.build_note: Decorated USC champion who never secured a long-term NFL starting job.

ratings_basis.signature: USC championship timing passer who could still move

players.name: Paxton Lynch
players.build_note: First-round traits bet who lost the job quickly and exited Denver after two seasons.

players.name: Rick Mirer
players.build_note: Rookie of the Year buzz that never turned into sustained production.

players.name: Robert Griffin III
players.build_note: Historic rookie season followed by major injuries and a rapid fall from franchise-quarterback expectations.

ratings_basis.signature: 2012 dual-threat MVP peak before the knee

players.name: Ryan Leaf
players.build_note: Drafted one pick after Peyton Manning; attitude/performance flameout became the bust-comparison standard.

ratings_basis.signature: cannon-armed Washington State prospect with processing collapse

players.name: Tim Couch
players.build_note: Expansion-era Browns' franchise QB who never developed behind a bad line.

ratings_basis.signature: Kentucky timing passer with pocket toughness

players.name: Todd Marinovich
players.build_note: "Robo QB," raised from birth to be an NFL passer; career derailed by off-field issues.

ratings_basis.signature: rehearsed short-game mechanics, modest arm talent

players.name: Courtney Brown
players.build_note: Penn State star, injuries limited him to a middling career.

players.name: Derrick Harvey
players.build_note: Jacksonville traded up for a pass rusher who produced eight sacks for the club.

ratings_basis.signature: Florida athletic edge with unfinished power

players.name: Jamaal Anderson
players.build_note: Drafted as a premier edge threat but recorded only 7.5 career sacks.

players.name: Vernon Gholston
players.build_note: Freak-athlete combine performer who finished his NFL career with zero sacks.

players.name: Aaron Curry
players.build_note: Marketed as the draft's safest prospect, then traded midway through his third season.

players.name: Isaiah Wilson
players.build_note: Played only a handful of snaps before off-field issues ended his Tennessee tenure.

players.name: Kyle Brady
players.build_note: Long blocking career, but never the impact receiving weapon expected from a top-ten tight end.

players.name: Rickey Dudley
players.archetype: TE / power runner + vertical receiver + inconsistent hands + consistency concern
players.build_note: Elite physical tools and occasional big plays were undermined by inconsistency and drops.

players.name: Charles Rogers
players.archetype: WR / open-field speed + injury risk + consistency concern
players.build_note: Michigan State star, injuries and off-field issues ended his career fast.

players.name: David Terrell
players.build_note: Michigan star who never cleared 700 receiving yards in a season.

players.name: Freddie Mitchell
players.build_note: First-round confidence and memorable quotes far outpaced his 90 career catches.

players.name: John Ross
players.build_note: Record-setting combine speed produced only flashes and persistent availability problems.

players.name: Kevin White
players.archetype: WR / open-field speed + power rusher + injury risk
players.build_note: Rare size-speed prospect whose career was overwhelmed by repeated injuries.

players.name: Matthew Jones
players.build_note: Arkansas quarterback drafted as a traits-based receiver experiment that never matured.

ratings_basis.signature: Arkansas big-play speed with drop issues

players.name: Peter Warrick
players.build_note: Florida State playmaker, never became the featured NFL weapon expected.

players.name: Rashaun Woods
players.build_note: Record-setting Oklahoma State receiver who caught only seven NFL passes.

players.name: Reggie Williams
players.build_note: Prototype frame and college production never developed into a dependable top target.

players.name: Troy Williamson
players.build_note: Drafted to replace Randy Moss; chronic drops defined his tenure.

ratings_basis.signature: track-speed deep threat with drop issues

players.name: Nate Robinson
players.build_note: Started games at cornerback for Washington and was an elite prep RB/DB/returner. A speed-and-return build is supported by real football tape, not just NBA athleticism.

players.name: Brock Lesnar
players.archetype: DT / open-field speed + power runner + championship poise
players.build_note: NCAA heavyweight champion who reached Vikings preseason camp without a conventional football background. His size and explosiveness justify a powerful but technically raw interior defender.

players.name: Dustin Byfuglien
players.build_note: Played NHL hockey at roughly 260 pounds with unusual movement skills and contact power; a credible penetrating-DT physical projection.

players.name: Gable Steveson
players.build_note: Olympic and NCAA champion signed by Buffalo as a defensive tackle despite never playing organized football; elite leverage and burst, raw technique.

players.name: Leati Anoa'i
players.build_note: A multi-year Georgia Tech defensive lineman who had brief pro-football stops before wrestling; a much firmer football basis than a physique-only celebrity pick. Game input: Leati Anoa'i.

players.name: Anthony Edwards
players.build_note: Played running back when young and has described football as his first sporting love; explosive acceleration and contact balance make HB the best fantasy translation.

players.name: Jackie Robinson
players.archetype: HB / open-field speed + decorated college star + special-teams ace
players.build_note: Football may have been his best UCLA sport: honorable-mention All-American, 12.2 yards per carry in 1939, and a national leader as a punt returner.

players.name: Louis Rees-Zammit
players.build_note: International rugby wing who entered the NFL pathway and spent time with Kansas City and Jacksonville; open-field speed and return ability are directly translatable.

players.name: Marcus Dupree
players.build_note: Generational Oklahoma freshman talent whose path through the USFL and injuries prevented the anticipated NFL career; a powerful pre-injury what-if profile.

players.name: Darin Erstad
players.build_note: Nebraska national-championship punter who averaged 42.6 yards per punt and also handled placekicking; an excellent special-teams addition.

players.name: Adam Dunn
players.build_note: Star Texas high-school quarterback who went to the University of Texas on a football scholarship before committing fully to baseball.

players.name: Allen Iverson
players.build_note: Quarterbacked Bethel to a Virginia state title, also played DB/KR, and was rated the nation's top high-school QB before choosing basketball.

players.name: Anders Lee
players.build_note: Two-year high-school starting QB, Minnesota Gatorade Football Player of the Year, and a Mr. Football finalist who received college offers in both football and hockey.

players.name: Archie Bradley
players.build_note: Elite prep quarterback who accepted an Oklahoma football scholarship before signing as the seventh MLB draft pick. Strong arm and power-running potential.

players.name: Carl Crawford
players.build_note: One of the most heavily recruited high-school quarterbacks in his class and held a Nebraska football offer before signing in baseball.

players.name: Charlie Ward
players.build_note: The strongest lock in the category: 1993 Heisman winner, national-title QB, and first-round Knicks pick who chose an 11-year NBA career instead of pursuing the NFL.

players.name: Chris Weinke
players.archetype: QB / pocket operator + decorated college star
players.build_note: Won the Heisman at age 28 after a baseball detour, then struggled as an NFL starter; mature pocket traits with deliberately modest athletic upside.

ratings_basis.signature: Florida State pocket veteran, late bloomer

players.name: Colt Brennan
players.archetype: QB / power runner + pocket operator + decorated college star + production profile
players.build_note: Record-setting Hawaii passer and Heisman finalist who never reached an NFL regular-season roster; spread accuracy and anticipation over arm power.

players.name: Danny Wuerffel
players.archetype: QB / pocket operator + decorated college star
players.build_note: Florida Heisman winner and elite college distributor whose game did not translate to sustained NFL starting success.

ratings_basis.signature: timing-and-touch distributor without a power arm

players.name: Derek Starling
players.build_note: Rushed for 2,471 yards and 31 TDs as a senior QB and passed up Nebraska football/baseball for the Royals. Game input: Derek Starling.

players.name: Donavan Tate
players.build_note: Nationally sought two-sport prospect committed to play QB at North Carolina before becoming MLB's third overall pick; later returned to college football.

players.name: Eric Crouch
players.build_note: 2001 Heisman-winning Nebraska option QB whose attempted NFL conversion to receiver never produced a regular-season appearance. Keep him at his authentic college position.

players.name: Gino Torretta
players.archetype: QB / pocket operator + decorated college star
players.build_note: Miami Heisman and national-title quarterback who received minimal NFL playing time; ratings should reflect college command rather than pro production.

players.name: Jalen Suggs
players.build_note: Four-star dual-threat with more than a dozen football offers; Minnesota Mr. Football after passing for 2,213 yards and rushing for 978 as a senior.

players.name: Jason White
players.archetype: QB / injury risk + decorated college star
players.build_note: Oklahoma Heisman winner whose knee history and lack of NFL measurables left him undrafted and without a regular-season career.

players.name: Joe Mauer
players.build_note: National high-school player of the year in football, threw for more than 5,500 yards and 73 TDs over two seasons, and signed with Florida State before baseball won out.

players.name: Major Harris
players.archetype: QB / mobile quarterback + decorated college star
players.build_note: West Virginia dual-threat and Heisman runner-up who went undrafted and received only a brief NFL opportunity; an early modern scramble/playmaking archetype.

players.name: Todd Helton
players.build_note: Tennessee scholarship quarterback who started games before Peyton Manning emerged; a legitimate college passer rather than a physique projection.

players.name: Tommie Frazier
players.build_note: Two-time Nebraska national champion and iconic option quarterback whose style and health never led to an NFL role. Elite option instincts and running vision.

players.name: Troy Smith
players.archetype: QB / pocket operator + mobile quarterback + decorated college star + tough competitor
players.build_note: Ohio State Heisman winner whose size and opportunity limited him mostly to backup work; mobile, competitive, and strongest outside a traditional pocket build.

players.name: Ty Detmer
players.archetype: QB / pocket operator + technical polish + decorated college star + production profile
players.build_note: Record-setting BYU Heisman passer whose pro career settled into long-term backup duty; a cerebral accuracy build with limited arm strength and athleticism.

players.name: Ilona Maher
players.build_note: Elite open-field tackling, contact balance, and ball skills translate naturally to strong safety; a valuable women's-sports crossover and a genuinely distinctive card.

players.name: Dave Winfield
players.build_note: The Vikings drafted the 6-foot-6, 230-pound Winfield despite his not playing college football. He was drafted in MLB, NBA, ABA, and NFL, making him the category's ultimate raw-athlete projection.

players.name: Frank Thomas
players.build_note: Entered Auburn on a football scholarship and played tight end before an injury and his baseball ceiling redirected him. At 6-foot-5 and roughly 275 pounds, the projection is unusually concrete.

ratings_basis.signature: Big Hurt play-strength mismatch at tight end

players.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
players.build_note: Length, movement, transition speed, and catch radius suggest a field-stretching TE; entirely projection-based and therefore appropriately raw in technique.

players.name: Joel Embiid
players.build_note: Length, strength, coordination, and catch radius create a red-zone specialist; durability and football technique prevent an overpowered build.

players.name: Jonah Lomu
players.archetype: TE / open-field speed + power runner + power rusher
players.build_note: Rugby's iconic size-speed collision: roughly edge-player mass with breakaway pace. A devastating receiving/power TE projection with raw routes and blocking technique.

players.name: Shaquille O'Neal
players.build_note: The ultimate goal-line mismatch and blocker by frame and explosiveness, but route running, stamina, and football awareness must keep him from becoming an automatic superstar.

players.name: Wilt Chamberlain
players.build_note: Generational size, speed, leaping, and strength made him a plausible red-zone TE/edge projection. Include as a projection, not as a fabricated football veteran.

players.name: Zdeno Chara
players.build_note: At 6-foot-9 with exceptional endurance and physicality, he projects as a red-zone target and engulfing blocker, tempered by change-of-direction limitations.

players.name: Zion Williamson
players.build_note: Rare mass and explosion make TE intuitive, but this is a pure projection with raw route running, blocking technique, and awareness.

ratings_basis.signature: Duke burst and play strength at TE

players.name: Carl Lewis
players.build_note: Dallas drafted the nine-time Olympic champion as a receiver in 1984 despite no college football experience; the obvious all-speed deep-threat/return-specialist build.

players.name: Jeff Francoeur
players.build_note: Won state football titles and declined a Clemson football scholarship after Atlanta drafted him; MLB records identify wide receiver as his projected college position.

players.name: Jeff Samardzija
players.build_note: Notre Dame All-American receiver with NFL size who was viewed as a legitimate pro prospect, but chose a long MLB pitching career.

players.name: John Havlicek
players.build_note: All-state high-school quarterback whom Cleveland drafted and tried at receiver before his Celtics career; an actual NFL camp participant.

players.name: Justin Gatlin
players.build_note: Olympic sprint champion who received NFL workouts and a Buccaneers tryout; another legitimate speed experiment, though less complete than Carl Lewis.

players.name: Kirk Gibson
players.build_note: First-team All-American and eventual College Football Hall of Famer at Michigan State; finished his college career as the school's leader in catches and receiving yards.

players.name: LeBron James
players.build_note: Played wide receiver through his junior year and earned first-team all-state honors; size, catch radius, and open-field power make WR more grounded than the usual speculative TE label.

players.name: Matt Barnes
players.archetype: WR / possession receiver + decorated college star
players.build_note: High-school All-American receiver with 58 catches, 1,112 yards, and 28 touchdowns as a senior; a credible big slot/possession receiver.

players.name: Usain Bolt
players.archetype: WR / open-field speed + possession receiver + durable competitor + tough competitor
players.build_note: The pure what-if selection: unmatched straight-line speed and public NFL interest, but no football resume. Ratings should pair elite speed with modest hands, route running, awareness, and toughness.

players.name: Earl Wilkinson
players.archetype: CB / open-field speed + zone ballhawk + special-teams ace
players.build_note: Former star corner and returner in *The Replacements*; a ballhawk/return-specialist defensive entry.

players.name: Stefen Djordjevic
players.build_note: The gifted two-way defensive back in *All the Right Moves* expands the pool with an iconic football-film role and a coverage/return profile.

players.name: Dalip Singh
players.archetype: DT / open-field speed + power runner + big hitter
players.build_note: *The Longest Yard*'s enormous enforcer; a maximum-strength, low-speed interior defender. Use Dalip Singh for the game-input name.

players.name: Dave Bautista
players.build_note: A natural nose/interior power defender: exceptional strength and mass, limited lateral agility and stamina.

players.name: Dwayne Johnson
players.build_note: More than stunt casting: Johnson was a 6-foot-5 Miami defensive tackle, backed up Warren Sapp, and later portrayed a retired NFL player in *Ballers*.

players.name: Ed O'Neill
players.build_note: Played college football and reached Steelers camp before acting. A stout interior run defender is the natural fictional treatment.

players.name: Tim Riggins
players.build_note: The bruising Dillon fullback/running back; ideal for trucking, stiff-arm, blocking, and short-yardage utility.

players.name: Dean Cain
players.build_note: Played safety at Princeton and signed with Buffalo before a knee injury. A coverage/instincts build grounded in real experience.

players.name: Boobie Miles
players.build_note: The electric Permian back in the film adaptation of *Friday Night Lights*; explosive pre-injury ratings create a true what-if card.

ratings_basis.signature: Friday Night Lights home-run back before the knee

players.name: Brian Williams
players.archetype: HB / open-field speed + power runner + undersized playmaker
players.build_note: Dillon's ambitious feature back in the *Friday Night Lights* series; a compact speed/power blend.

players.name: Burt Reynolds
players.build_note: Played halfback at Florida State before knee injuries ended a promising career, then became the defining star of the original *The Longest Yard*.

players.name: Christopher Bridges
players.archetype: HB / open-field speed + elusive runner + receiving back + undersized playmaker
players.build_note: Compact, agile, and fast-paced public persona fits an elusive receiving back and return option. Game input: Christopher Bridges.

players.name: Darnell Jefferson
players.build_note: Explosive freshman tailback in *The Program*; speed and open-field ability make him one of the better college-fiction entries.

players.name: Earl Megget
players.build_note: The elusive back from *The Longest Yard* remake; a speed/change-of-direction complement to the heavier backs.

players.name: Ernie Davis
players.archetype: HB / open-field speed + power runner + decorated college star
players.build_note: Portrayal of the first Black Heisman winner in *The Express*; a historically grounded power-and-speed runner.

players.name: Forrest Gump
players.build_note: Alabama return specialist whose fictional straight-line speed drove the football portion of *Forrest Gump*. Best implemented at HB with elite return ratings.

players.name: Julian Washington
players.build_note: The established feature back in *Any Given Sunday*; gives the screen group a power runner instead of another quarterback.

players.name: Kevin Hart
players.build_note: Natural novelty return specialist: very small frame, elite acceleration and change of direction, but severe carrying, blocking, and break-tackle limitations.

players.name: Nigel Gruff
players.archetype: K / pocket operator + zone ballhawk + accurate kicker
players.build_note: Soccer-player-turned-kicker in *The Replacements* with absurd range, plus accuracy/awareness volatility. Adds needed special-teams flavor.

players.name: Chris Hemsworth
players.build_note: Edge-rusher fantasy build driven by length, strength, pursuit, and explosiveness; technique and football awareness keep it balanced.

players.name: Alvin Mack
players.archetype: MLB / power runner + run stopper + big hitter + consistency concern
players.build_note: Fearsome linebacker in *The Program*; elite hit power and pursuit, with personality-driven discipline penalties reflected through awareness.

players.name: Bobby Boucher
players.build_note: *The Waterboy*'s tackling phenomenon; a pursuit, hit-power, and block-shedding novelty build with deliberately low awareness.

players.name: Brian Banks
players.build_note: Portrayal of the elite linebacker prospect whose career was stolen by a wrongful conviction; ratings should reflect his documented prep potential.

players.name: Daniel Bateman
players.build_note: The hyper-aggressive defensive captain in *The Replacements*; a hit-power/run-stopper build.

players.name: John Cena
players.build_note: Played center in college before wrestling and acting; translate that football experience into a powerful downhill middle linebacker with strong awareness and tackling.

players.name: O'Shea Jackson
players.archetype: MLB / run stopper + durable competitor + consistency concern + undersized playmaker + tough competitor
players.build_note: A compact, forceful middle-linebacker fantasy card built around tackling, toughness, block shedding, and attitude. Game input: O'Shea Jackson.

players.name: Steve Austin
players.build_note: The guards' intimidating defensive leader in *The Longest Yard*; downhill power and tackling over coverage ability. Use Steve Austin for the game-input name.

players.name: Aubrey Graham
players.archetype: QB / pocket operator + mobile quarterback + durable competitor + tough competitor
players.build_note: Former actor and rapper cast as a rhythm passer: strong short accuracy and play-action presence, modest toughness and scrambling. Game input: Aubrey Graham.

players.name: Flash Gordon
players.build_note: The character is introduced as a former New York Jets quarterback before becoming a sci-fi hero; an especially playful celeb-category fit.

players.name: Jack Rooney
players.build_note: The veteran Sharks quarterback in *Any Given Sunday*; a natural pocket-passer/captain contrast to Beamen.

players.name: Jimmy Dix
players.build_note: Disgraced former pro quarterback from *The Last Boy Scout*; a veteran arm-talent reclamation build.

players.name: Joe Kane
players.build_note: Gifted but troubled college quarterback from *The Program*; strong arm and mobility with volatile awareness.

players.name: Joe Kingman
players.build_note: Superstar Boston quarterback in *The Game Plan*. A strong-armed power-QB build distinct from Johnson's separate real-life DT card.

players.name: Joe Pendleton
players.build_note: Rams quarterback in *Heaven Can Wait*; a classic-film inclusion that expands the category beyond modern comedy.

players.name: Jonathan Moxon
players.build_note: Cerebral backup-turned-starter from *Varsity Blues*; accuracy and awareness over raw arm strength.

players.name: Lance Harbor
players.build_note: West Canaan's highly recruited star quarterback in *Varsity Blues*; stronger arm and athletic ceiling than Mox, balanced by the career-altering knee injury.

players.name: Mark Harmon
players.build_note: A real two-year UCLA starting quarterback before acting fame. The fictional card can lean on authentic accuracy, mobility, and leadership rather than pure invention.

players.name: Paul Blake
players.build_note: Aging former high-school star recruited to quarterback Texas State in *Necessary Roughness*; smart veteran passer with limited athleticism.

players.name: Paul Crewe
players.build_note: The original portrayal is the selected version. Reynolds' real FSU background gives the character extra credibility; Sandler is represented separately as Bobby Boucher.

players.name: Shane Falco
players.build_note: The replacement quarterback at the center of *The Replacements*; one of the most recognizable fictional pro-football QBs.

players.name: Vince Howard
players.archetype: QB / elusive runner + mobile quarterback + raw traits
players.build_note: Raw athlete developed into East Dillon's star dual-threat QB; high upside with ratings built around growth and improvisation.

players.name: Willie Beamen
players.archetype: QB / open-field speed + elusive runner + mobile quarterback
players.build_note: The explosive third-stringer turned starter in *Any Given Sunday*; an ideal improvisational, mobile-QB build.

players.name: Rudy Ruettiger
players.archetype: RE / durable competitor + consistency concern + tough competitor
players.build_note: The quintessential effort player from *Rudy*; very low size/athletic ceiling but exceptional motor, toughness, and pursuit.

players.name: Terry Crews
players.build_note: A genuine NFL defensive end/linebacker who became a major actor and returned to football comedy in *The Longest Yard*; the cleanest literal "celeb who was an NFL player" fit.

players.name: Vernon Littlefield
players.build_note: The Cowboys defensive end in *Ballers*. Carter was also a UCLA defensive lineman before injuries ended his own playing career.

players.name: Bill Goldberg
players.build_note: The former NFL lineman and wrestler's *Longest Yard* role supplies a celebrity interior blocker with authentic size and power. Use Bill Goldberg for the game-input name.

players.name: Billy Bob
players.build_note: Use Billy as the first name and Bob as the last name in-game; a huge, powerful West Canaan lineman whose strength is offset by stamina and agility limitations.

players.name: Charles Greane
players.build_note: The retired Dolphins lineman in *Ballers* who attempts a comeback at right tackle; useful representation at a position novelty lists usually ignore.

players.name: Jumbo Fumiko
players.build_note: Sumo wrestler converted to offensive tackle in *The Replacements*; massive strength and run blocking balanced by poor agility.

players.name: Clifford Smith
players.archetype: SS / open-field speed + power runner + zone ballhawk + big hitter
players.build_note: A physical strong-safety persona: hit power, press coverage, and intimidation, with restrained top-end speed. Game input: Clifford Smith.

players.name: Idris Elba
players.build_note: Veteran defensive captain archetype with awareness, zone coverage, tackling, and leadership rather than extreme speed.

players.name: Brian Murphy
players.build_note: *The Replacements*' gifted Gallaudet tight end and game-winning target; a balanced possession TE.

players.name: Jason Momoa
players.build_note: Size and action-star athleticism fit an inline power TE specializing in contested catches, stiff arms, and run blocking.

players.name: Calvin Broadus
players.build_note: Deep football connection as a longtime youth coach and league founder; make him a smooth possession receiver with good awareness and hands. Game input: Calvin Broadus.

players.name: Charlie Tweeder
players.archetype: WR / possession receiver + undersized playmaker + tough competitor
players.build_note: The undersized, fearless slot receiver from *Varsity Blues*; separation, spectacular catches, and swagger over size or blocking.

players.name: Clifford Franklin
players.build_note: *The Replacements* speedster who can separate from anyone but initially cannot catch; a perfect extreme speed-versus-hands archetype.

players.name: Cornell Haynes
